events.headline: Clay adds workflow credit limits, MCP controls and contact-deletion APIs
events.summary: Released workflow spending caps, domain-based MCP client allowlisting and APIs to permanently delete Audiences contacts.

events.headline: Auto-mode becomes the default for new Claygents
events.summary: New Claygents automatically select an AI model for each research row to balance quality and cost; existing Claygents retain their models.

events.headline: Clay releases SCIM provisioning and expands Audiences and search capabilities
events.summary: Added identity-provider provisioning, Audiences record upserts, signal-to-workflow handoffs and metro-area search.

events.headline: Enterprise pricing page gains governance and security features
events.summary: A dated comparison detected new Enterprise feature listings for user groups, SCIM, IP allowlists, connection controls and workflow/workbook limits; no list-price increase was recorded.

events.headline: Clay redesigns its home page and improves Audiences and Ads reporting
events.summary: Introduced a refreshed home page, consolidated Audiences sources and exports, and more accurate advertising audience-size and match-rate reporting.

events.headline: G2 announces direct access to its intelligence within Clay
events.summary: G2 announced a partnership bringing reviews, market intelligence and buying signals into Clay workflows, accessible with Clay credits without a separate G2 subscription.

events.headline: Clay announces an agent-first experience and Inbound SDR Agent
events.summary: Clay’s dated Sculpt recap announced an agent-first way to build in Clay alongside the Inbound SDR Agent.

events.headline: Clay adds workflow budgets, bulk reruns and Ads CLI commands
events.summary: Added workflow credit budgets, bulk workflow reruns, trusted-domain workspace access, Ads management through the CLI and redesigned Audiences record details.

events.headline: Clay launches its Skills Marketplace
events.summary: Launched a library of community-built skills that sales and revenue teams can install free and run in their own Clay accounts.

events.headline: Clay expands its data-provider and action integrations
events.summary: Added new and upgraded integrations that broaden GTM data sourcing, enrichment, buying signals and downstream actions.

events.headline: Clay expands Ads audience management and adds IP access restrictions
events.summary: Added LinkedIn company-list targeting, recurring ad-sync editing and history, plus workspace IP restrictions covering browser and API/MCP access.

excerpts: [Article – NY Times Clay allows employees to sell shares at a $5b valuation.![](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/61702af2e3966e09c4101538/69a1f1f3a080096c6cf4cbfa_company-ads-v0.avif)](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/01/28/business/dealbook/clay-start-up-tender-offers.html?unlocked_article_code=1.H1A.LBNX.YbS98P3kIG8Q&smid=url-share) [Get a demo](https://www.clay.com/demo) [Sign up](https://app.clay.com/signup?source=nav) [All changelogs](https://www.clay.com/changelog) / [Product Roundup Week of September 21, 2026](https://www.clay.com/changelog/product-roundup-week-of-september-21-2026) September 28, 2026 Product Roundup Week of September 21, 2026 Clay Ads A set of improvements to Clay Ads makes ad audiences easier to manage at scale. Send **company lists** to LinkedIn for targeting, in addition to people-based audiences. **Pause** and **edit** recurring Ad Syncs instead of rebuilding them from scratch. Review **Sync history** in-product to see what ran, when, and what happened. Filter the **Ads** home page by provider and see export destinations more clearly. Find migrated legacy audience-backed syncs in the **Ad Syncs** tab with a "Legacy ad sync" prefix; recurring syncs keep running. Together these make recurring ad programs easier to run and audit. [Learn more →](https://www.clay.com/ads) IP Access Restrictions Admins can now restrict the incoming IP addresses that workspace members connect from, in a few clicks. Open **Workspace Settings** and go to the **Security** subsection. In the **IP access restriction** card, define the IP addresses allowed to access the workspace. Apply the same restriction to incoming browser requests and to API/MCP requests. This gives security teams a simple way to keep workspace access inside approved networks.
